blocks.text: CyCognito is an exposure management platform that reduces risk by discovering, testing, and prioritizing security issues.
There are two CyCognito streams. Select those that are based on your CyCognito feature plan and use cases:

blocks.item: CyCognito Issues: Retrieves a detailed and actionable overview of security issues across your enterprise's digital assets.
CyCognito Assets: Retrieves a comprehensive view of your enterprise's digital assets.

blocks.text: The CyCognito connector is in limited availability. To learn more, contact Zscaler Support.
To configure the CyCognito connector, you need the source authentication configuration. The following parameters are required:

blocks.item: API Key
You must be an admin or an IT user to create a CyCognito API key.
To create an API key:
In the CyCognito portal, go to Workflow & Integration > API Key Management.
See image.
Click the Add API key icon.
See image.
The Generate new API key window appears.
In the Generate new API key window:
Key name: Enter name for the API key.
Key access: Select Read only.
Set expiration: (Optional) Enable and set an expiration date for the API key.
If an expiration date is set on the API key, make sure to refresh the key when it expires to ensure continuous connectivity.
Click Create.
See image.
Copy the generated API key.
Save the API key securely as you cannot copy or view it later.
URL
The base URL of your CyCognito instance prefixed with api.
Examples include:
https://api.cycognito.com
https://api.platform.cycognito.com
https://api.us-platform.cycognito.com

blocks.text: To create the CyCognito data source in the Zscaler Security Operations (SecOps) platform:

blocks.item: Go to Configure > Sources.
Click Create.
Search for and select the connector tile from the available data sources.
See image.

blocks.text: After you create the CyCognito data source, enter the following information in the source setup Retrieval section:

blocks.item: Authentication
To configure authentication:
In the Authentication section, click Create New.
The CyCognito Authentication window appears.
In the CyCognito Authentication window, enter the information from the Prerequisites section.
See image.
Click Create.
To learn more, see Configuring Authentications and Managing Authentications.
Assets Type
Select the type of assets that you want to include in the scope of the ingested data. Asset types include IP addresses, domains, certificates, web applications, and IP address ranges.
This filter is available in the CyCognito Assets stream.
Asset Status (Optional)
Select the asset statuses you want to include in the scope of the ingested data. If left empty, the connector defaults to retrieving only assets with a new status. Available statuses are:
New: Recently discovered by CyCognito and not yet seen in a previous scan.
Changed: The asset has been modified, or its properties have changed since the last scan.
Normal: The asset is known, active, and unchanged since the last scan.
Removed: The asset is no longer detected on your attack surface (inactive or decommissioned).
This filter is available in the CyCognito Assets stream.
Issues Status (Optional)

Select the issue statuses that you want to include in the scope of the ingested data. If left empty, the connector defaults to retrieving only issues with a new status. Available statuses are New, Normal, Issue-Removed, Asset-Removed, and Asset-Not-Alive.
This drop-down menu is available in the CyCognito Issues stream.

blocks.text: For complete configuration instructions, see Creating Data Sources.
